runs.title: Josh Jacobs: what actually happened?
runs.prompt: Today is Sunday 11 October 2026, and Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs is trending amid reports of legal issues and questions over whether he plays in the Week 5 game against the Chicago Bears. Find out what actually happened with his legal issues and whether he is playing today. Start with the pages below.
runs.answer: Josh Jacobs is NOT playing today. His legal issues: he was arrested in May 2026 over an incident involving his ex-girlfriend and was formally charged with two misdemeanors (battery and criminal damage to property); on Sept. 10, 2026 he pleaded no contest — he was found guilty of battery and fined $1,000 plus costs, and got a deferred judgment on the criminal-damage charge (12 months of conditions including no contact with the victim, supervision, counseling and restitution). The NFL placed him on the Commissioner's Exempt List (paid administrative leave) on Aug. 30; players on that list cannot practice or attend/play games, so he has missed every game and will sit out the Week 5 Bears game at Lambeau on Oct. 11. He remains on the list (41 days as of Oct. 11) while the league's personal-conduct investigation continues, held up in part by its request for surveillance video of the incident that the victim is trying to seal under Wisconsin's Marsy's Law; a standard domestic-violence suspension is six games, and exempt-list time would count retroactively.

runs.title: England's early flu season: what UKHSA says
runs.prompt: UKHSA is trending in England with reports that flu cases in September 2026 were higher than usual. Find out what UKHSA actually says about September flu levels, whether this counts as an early flu season, and where the official numbers are published. Start with the pages below.
runs.answer: UKHSA confirms that flu activity throughout September 2026 was higher than in the same period of all the previous 4 winters, but stresses levels were still at "baseline" (very low) and had been trending upward since August. In its first weekly winter surveillance report (covering week 40, 28 Sep–4 Oct 2026, published 8 October), influenza activity had risen and was circulating at baseline, with test positivity up to 6.5% from 5.0% the previous week and flu hospitalisations at 1.97 per 100,000; the rise was driven mainly by 18–24-year-olds. On the "early season" question UKHSA only goes as far as "possible signs"/"early signs" — it says that IF the upward trend continues it "suggests an early flu season," i.e. it does not yet declare one, and flags a "drifted" A(H1N1) strain. The official numbers are published in the weekly National flu and COVID-19 surveillance reports on GOV.UK (https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/national-flu-and-covid-19-surveillance-reports-2026-to-2027-season, with HTML report, PDF graphs and ODS data files) and on the UKHSA data dashboard (https://ukhsa-dashboard.data.gov.uk/respiratory-viruses/influenza), supported by the news story and the UKHSA blog p
